So my required equity is about 24%, but a flush draw alone gives me roughly 19.5% on the river. I need to factor in my overcards—A and Q—but they're likely not clean outs if he's holding an overpair or a set. His aggressive line suggests he has something strong, probably an overpair or a set, which means my overcards don't help much. I'm essentially relying on the flush draw, which falls short of the pot odds I need. Reconsidering his range—he could have a flush draw, top pair, or an overpair given his aggressive 3bet from early position. Against hands like AK (which would be a bluff here), I'm actually ahead with my ace-high and flush draw, and against top pair I need the flush. Blending in the possibility of bluffs and worse hands, my equity looks closer to 30%, and with the pot odds around 3.2:1 (needing 24%), calling makes sense.
